text:
sam (support): Hey team — customer reported batch rerank returns where scores are shifted by one candidate for queries after the 3rd query. Payload looks fine to them but results don't align with per-query candidates. attaching snippet.

bailey (eng-ml): Can you paste the minimal request they used? is it JSON or ndjson/csv?

sam (support): They sent application/json via our API. minimal:```json
{
  "queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3", "q4"],
  "candidates": [["a","b"],["c"],["d","e","f"],["g"]]
}
``` but server returned scores that map as if candidates arrays were flattened then shifted starting at q3.

nina (qa): Any chance one of the inner arrays had a null or empty string in the real payload? that can trip our parser if the content-type doesn't match.

sam (support): customer confirmed one candidate was an empty string for q3 in the original CSV they converted. they said they used our python client which does an automatic conversion.

bailey (eng-ml): Hmm -- our batching layer expects strictly nested lists. Historically, when the python client sends ndjson we treat each line as a separate request; when sending JSON the conversion should preserve inner empty strings, but there was a recent optimization where we run a prefix flattening step for zero-length elements to compress tokens. that could cause an off-by-one on candidate offsets if an inner element is empty.

alex (eng): Can you capture the raw bytes for the request/response (request_id)? deploy-bot can provide logs if we have the id.

sam (support): request_id: req_20240217_8a9c. deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: Retrieved logs for req_20240217_8a9c — payload received: content-type: application/json; body-length: 2.1KB. showing candidates array where one entry is "" (empty string).

bailey (eng-ml): Reproduced locally with that payload — I can reproduce the misalignment when an inner candidate is an empty string and the request goes through batching with "compact_empty" optimization enabled.

nina (qa): Quick repro steps for support: 1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json 2) payload.json uses nested candidate lists with one empty string 3) Observe that starting at the query after the empty candidate, scores are applied to wrong candidates.

sam (support): Customer is asking for either a workaround or an ETA. they are blocked in production.

bailey (eng-ml): Immediate workaround: remove empty-string candidates (filter x -> x != ""). Our server will accept that and alignment is preserved. Also recommend sending candidates as explicit objects with ids: ```json
{
  "queries": [..],
  "candidates": [[{"id": "c1", "text": "a"}], [{"id": "c2", "text": ""}], ...]
}
``` the id binding prevents relying on positional offsets.

alex (eng): I'll open a patch. Root cause: the compact_empty optimization removes zero-length payloads during the continuous batch flattening step but doesn't adjust per-query offsets correctly. Need to either disable compaction for nested arrays or carry an explicit offset map.

bailey (eng-ml): Proposed fix: change batcher to emit an offsets array alongside flattened candidates: offsets: [2,1,3,1] so servers can map scores deterministically even if compaction runs. adding tests.

nina (qa): I'll add a regression test to the rerank suite with mixed empty strings, nulls, and varying lengths.

sam (support): Customer accepted workaround for now, asked for ETA. any estimate?

bailey (eng-ml): I can have a hotfix that disables compact_empty for nested candidate requests in the next deploy window (ETA 6 hours). full offsets-mapping change will be in next minor (ETA 3 days).

sam (support): Perfect — I'll relay that. also attaching the minimal failing payload so customers can try the filter workaround.

alex (eng): Patch landed to disable compaction for nested candidate requests. rolling out now. will monitor.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary -> 2 nodes. changelist: disable compact_empty for rerank nested lists (hotfix).

bailey (eng-ml): Post-deploy notes: verified canary with original failing payload; mapping restored. preparing changelog and SDK note advising to avoid empty-string candidates or include ids.

sam (support): Thanks — I'll follow up with the customer and close the escalation once they confirm. closing steps: share workaround, ETA, and link to PR when available. :thumbsup:

nina (qa): PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5123 — tests added for empty candidate alignment.

bailey (eng-ml): Follow-up: internal ticket RND-2345 created for offsets-array enhancement.

sam (support): closing loop — customer confirmed fix works after we asked them to strip empty candidates while we rolled the hotfix. they will update their CSV export. thanks all.
